Ellen (People Ops): Heads up 11 New hire Nisha is on OPT EAD that expires 2026-05-20 and we've offered 2026-05-10 start. She says her STEM OPT renewal + H-1B cap filing will be in motion. Can we onboard before expiry?
Luis (Recruiter): Nisha confirmed she has a current valid EAD today (physically in hand). She can present it at I-9. But her renewal is pending and H-1B filing may take months.
Jared (Hiring Manager): We want her in asap. Team ramp week begins 5/17. Any blocker if we start 5/10?
Priya (Immigration Counsel): TL;DR: If she has a currently valid EAD on 5/10, she can be employed through the EAD expiration date. For STEM OPT holders who timely file an EAD renewal, there used to be an automatic 180-day extension (recent rule changes vary), but always confirm category and filing type. For H-1B cap with change of status, timing matters.
Nisha (Candidate): I have my physical OPT EAD (card) until 5/20. I plan to file timely for STEM extension (cap-gap) and my attorney will file H-1B if selected. I'm OK starting 5/10 but worried about payroll and benefits if renewal isn't approved quickly.
Sam (Payroll): Payroll needs a valid List A or List B+List C combination at the time of hire. If she presents the current EAD card on 5/10, that's fine. If she later has a pending EAD renewal, we may be able to rely on the receipt rule depending on USCIS guidance for her category. But for tax/SSN reporting we need to capture SSN and correct work authorization dates. If she later changes to H-1B with COS, we re-record the I-9.
Juno (Benefits): Benefits enrollment depends on HRIS hire date. Carriers accept the payroll roster. We typically enroll someone effective with first day of employment. If hire date is 5/10 and payroll is set, benefits can start then. If payroll is delayed, we can retro-enroll but it complicates premiums.
Ellen (People Ops): Action plan proposal: require Nisha to present EAD card in person during onboarding (I-9 section 2). We'll allow remote verification only if an authorized agent is used. We'll set hire date 5/10 and note "contingent on presenting valid docs". If renewal receipt is later provided, confirm with legal whether receipt creates extension.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Note: STEM OPT category is (c)(3)(C) historically and timely-filed STEM extension on Form I-765 often grants automatic extension but the exact days vary. New regs in 2024 changed some timelines; I will confirm whether the 180-day extension is still in effect for STEM and whether receipt rule applies to initial vs renewal filings.
Sam (Payroll): Also flag: if she gets an SSN after hire we must update ADP/Payroll and ensure W-2 reflects correct SSN. If she doesn't have SSN day one, payroll can still run but we need to set SSA reporting once available. Confirm candidate has SSN?
Nisha (Candidate): I already have an SSN from OPT, I'll upload it to the portal.
Luis (Recruiter): I'll schedule in-person onboarding with Ellen for 5/10 at 9am so she can show EAD (and passport) in person.
onboard-bot: Reminder: please upload required docs to the secure portal. Do not attach sensitive docs in channel.
Jared (Hiring Manager): If H-1B COS is approved later, do we need any action from the manager?
Priya (Immigration Counsel): If H-1B change of status is approved, USCIS issues approval notice (I-797). Employer should collect the new I-94 and update I-9 reverification or rehire steps as required. If change to H-1B occurs mid-payroll period, payroll/tax withholding stays same but benefit eligibility remains continuous. We will coordinate with payroll to handle re-verification on the I-9 when she provides H-1B docs.
Sam (Payroll): We'll need a new copy of the approval (H-1B I-797 and I-94) to retain. Also confirm worksite location; remote states may affect tax withholding.
Juno (Benefits): If she's in a waiting period, note that HSA/HRA contributions start based on carrier effective date. We'll handle any plan changes if her status affects eligibility (generally immigration status does not change eligibility, but payroll enrollment must be complete).
Ellen (People Ops): Okay curled up plan: 1) Nisha to present EAD card + passport on 5/10 in person for I-9. 2) Luis to confirm 5/10 in calendar. 3) Priya to confirm whether STEM renewal receipt grants automatic extension for work auth and advise if we can accept receipt for payroll in interim. 4) Sam to advise payroll steps for eventual H-1B COS (I-9 reverification checklist). 5) Juno to prepare benefits welcome packet with effective date 5/10 and instructions if any retro-change needed.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): I'll check recent USCIS memos and confirm on thread by tomorrow. Quick note 1: if employer files H-1B and requests premium processing, USCIS sends receipt that doesn't by itself create work authorization 1 that's separate. Premium only speeds adjudication.
Nisha (Candidate): Thanks 1 I'm uploading scans of EAD, passport and SSN card now. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Sam (Payroll): Received docs via portal. We'll set payroll to begin 5/10 provided I-9 Section 2 completed with the EAD. If H-1B COS happens later, please forward approval docs to payroll@.
Luis (Recruiter): All set on my end. Welcome aboard Nisha! :party_parrot:
Ellen (People Ops): Great 1 closing the loop: Priya if you confirm the STEM receipt extension rule isn't reliable, we'll still onboard on 5/10 because she has physical EAD. If the card expired before start we'd need to pause. Thanks team.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Confirmed via memo: timely-filed STEM extension renewal typically provides an auto-extension but given policy churn, we won't rely on a receipt if the candidate's card expires before start. In Nisha's case she has a valid card through 5/20 so proceed. I'll post a short checklist for reverification steps if/when her status switches to H-1B.
Ellen (People Ops): Perfect. Closing 1 See onboarding checklist updated in the People Ops drive.
Nisha (Candidate): Thank you all 1 excited to start 5/10!
